title: Two-sided Bernstein tail bound
statement:
Let $X : \Omega \to \bbr$ be a random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, and let $c, t_{\max} \ge 0$ be real parameters such that $X$ satisfies the Bernstein moment generating function condition with parameters $c$ and $t_{\max}$: for every $t$ with $\abs{t} \le t_{\max}$ the exponential moment $e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{tX}] \le e^{c t^2}$. If $c > 0$, then for every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2 c\, t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid s < \abs{X(\omega)}\}\bigr) \;\le\; 2\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: X satisfies the Bernstein MGF condition with parameters c and tmax
replaced:
Let $X$ satisfy $\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ X\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$
with $c > 0$.  For every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2c\,t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid s < |X(\omega)|\}\bigr) \;\le\;
  2\exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
